content.title: About
content.content: Chicken drumsticks are the lower leg portion of the bird, consisting of meat attached to a bone. In this preparation the skin is not eaten. Drumsticks are a good source of protein, B‑vitamins, and minerals such as iron and zinc.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Drumsticks are often used in dishes that require slow braising or roasting because they stay moist.
The bones are believed to contain collagen, which may benefit joints and skin.
In many cuisines chicken drumsticks are served as a snack after marinating in soy sauce and spices.
When the skin is left on it can become crispy, but this recipe omits the skin.
Drumsticks add a rich flavor to stocks and broths.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Provides essential amino acids needed for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamin source
items.content: Contains niacin, vitamin B6 and B12, which support metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Rich in minerals
items.content: Iron and zinc contribute to immune function and hemoglobin formation.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Suitable for low‑carb diets as it contains virtually no sugar.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Collagen from the bone may help maintain joint and bone strength.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken meat.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Drumsticks contain cholesterol, so people with high cholesterol should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Improper storage or undercooking can allow salmonella or campylobacter growth.

items.title: Bone hazards
items.content: The bone can pose a choking risk, especially for children.

items.title: Sodium in marinades
items.content: If marinated in salty solutions, sodium levels can become high.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook the skin‑less drumsticks by baking, boiling, braising, or grilling. After cooking, separate the meat from the bone and discard the bone. Serve with vegetables, sauces, or sliced in salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh drumsticks in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for up to 2 days. For longer storage freeze them in an airtight bag at –18 °C for up to 6 months. Discard any that develop an off‑odor or discoloration before cooking.
